title: Does a slightly different launch leave the orbit?
question: If you change the launch speed or direction a little, is it a crash, an orbit or an escape?
steps: Press the blue planet and pull it back.
Let go and it flies the opposite way.
Change the length and direction a little to find all three results.
observe: See how launches that look alike take different paths depending on the direction and the escape speed, and whether a bigger orbit radius makes a longer orbit period.

terms.name: Orbit
terms.description: The path of a thing moving around a body under its gravity.

terms.name: Universal gravitation
terms.description: The force with which all things with mass attract each other.

terms.name: Escape speed
terms.description: The smallest starting speed needed to get away from a body's gravity.

terms.name: Kepler's law
terms.description: Around the same central body, the bigger the orbit's radius, the longer its period.

law.title: Universal gravitation and Kepler's law
law.description: Gravity bends the direction of travel, and on a circular orbit the cube of the radius is proportional to the square of the period.

tip: Press the blue planet, pull it and let go: it flies the opposite way. The pull's direction is the launch direction (5° steps) and its length is the speed (0.1 m/s steps). Pick the start radius with the picture buttons.
tip_short: Pull the planet back and let go to launch

controls.label: Launch direction (90° = sideways counterclockwise, 0° = away from the star)

predict.question: Launched just right, what will the planet do?
predict.reason: The star pulls the planet. At just the right speed, it neither falls in nor leaves. It goes round and round.
predict.bridge: Launch it and see for yourself!

stages.text: Go around the star once, 4 meters away!
stages.say: The star's gravity pulls the planet. Launched just right, it doesn't fall in but goes round the star.

stages.text: Go around twice close to the star, at 2 meters!
stages.say: Close to the star, the gravity is strong. So it goes around faster.
stages.miss: Shoot it sideways, just right, from close by!

stages.text: From 4 meters, shoot it very hard to bring back the far piece!
stages.say: When it is very fast, the star's gravity can't hold it. Then the planet leaves the star and goes far away.
stages.win: Whoosh! It brought the piece back!

story.clue: One piece is floating far away in space! Let's shoot the planet and bring it back!
story.map_clue: The last one is at the island's highest lookout!

kid.intro: This is the star orbit lab. The star pulls the planet towards it. This force is **gravity** too. The planet runs sideways while the star pulls it in. Running just right, it goes round and round. Let's see how fast to shoot it so it goes around!
kid.title: Let's go round and round the star!
kid.say: The star pulls the planet and makes it go round and round. Close by, it goes around faster, and too fast, it leaves the star.
kid.tip: Pull the planet back and let go: it flies the other way!

note.law: The star's gravity pulls the planet and bends its path. At the circular orbit speed it goes round and round, and faster than the escape speed it leaves.
